- `pageMapProblems(rows, ajv?)` → schema problems, duplicate slugs and parents naming no row.
- `drawerRepeatsHeader(menu, megaLabels)` → true for a drawer-region draft menu whose top-level items are each a header mega item's label.

### `lib/intake-pagemap-owners.mjs`
- `ownedSurfaces(surfaces, rows, endpoints, routeSlug)` → `{ rows, parts: [{ row, part }] }`: the surfaces that become rows, and each other surface as a part of its owning row (null for the site chrome).
- `wooSlugs(rows, accountPages)`, `shopTitle(row, label)`, `wooPages(rows, surfaces, used)`: WooCommerce's slugs, the shop row's menu label, and the cart, checkout and my-account rows a shop client always has; `checkoutEndpoints(rows, route, pageOfTag, home, routeSlug, facts)` → the routes reached only from checkout that the checkout's submit leads to or that show an order reference (`facts` from `commerceFacts`), removed from the rows.

### `lib/intake-pagemap-commerce.mjs`
- `commerceFacts(exp, routeKeys, links)` → Map( route → { payment, orderLines, password, listing, reaches, submits, orderRef } ): what each routed page shows, read from its template and logic.
- `commerceKinds(rows, facts, gaps)`: gives each route row its shop, cart or checkout shape from the manifest's declaration (`row.declared`) or the structure; a word hint (`row.hint`) the structure does not bear out is a gap row. `declaredKind(type, kind)` → `'shop' | 'cart' | 'checkout' | null` from a manifest page's `wp.type` and `kind`.

### `lib/intake-pagemap-hints.mjs`
- `crossCheck(code, hint)` → `{ surfaces, gaps }`: the code surfaces with their `surfaces.json` pairings (by kind, a hint modal or form with a code choice flow, place and name), then the hint-only records, and one `surfaces-disagree` gap row per surface one side lacks.

### `lib/intake-pagemap-regen.mjs`
- `runPageMap(o, { log })` → exit code: `intake.mjs --page-map`, writing nothing when the regenerated map (or the intake record holding it) does not validate; it also puts the proposal into intake.json's `pageMap` and renders review.md again (`syncIntake`), so `--apply-review` confirms the regenerated map.
- `syncIntake(intake, proposal, { reviewText, day })` → `{ record, problems, refused }`: the saved intake record with `proposal` (the regenerated rows before marks and ids) as its page map and its review rows carried as a re-run carries them (review.md's unapplied marks, then every mark whose row is unchanged); `{ record: null }` for no record or a palette-only one.
- `pageMapMarks(intake)` → Map( rowId → mark ) of the page-map review rows; `applyMarks(rows, marks)` → `{ rows, applied, unapplied, refused, lost }` (`drop`, `edit:<field>=<value>` for an `EDITABLE` field; an empty or `null` parent or template clears it; `refused` lists edits of other fields, `lost` each dropped row's parts). `lostIds(current, rows, marks)` → the current rows holding an id the new map loses, except those dropped.
- `carryIds(rows, current)` → the rows with the current map's ids by row key; `mapChanges(before, after)` → `added <key>`, `removed <key>` and `<key>: <field> <before> -> <after>` lines.

### `lib/intake-pagemap-surfaces.mjs`
- `codeSurfaces(exp, routeOf, routeKeys?, links?)` → `{ surfaces, menus, formComponents, accountPages, pageOfTag }`: the CPT surfaces found in the code (each with `page`, an overlay also with `nav`, `orderLines` and `reaches`, the route keys its own links lead to), their menus, the route keys whose pages hold a password field, and `pageOfTag(draftId)` → the page holding an element id. `isChoiceFlow(node)` → two or more pick lists (no tabs or disclosures) and no `<form>`. `showsOrderLines(text, L, node)` → a loop inside the element binds a currency amount. `pageOf(d, node, routeKeys)` → the route whose page holds a template node. `KIND_POST_TYPE`: surface kind to post type.
- `elementTree`, `innerText`, `descendants`, `ancestors`, `kebab`, `stem`: template tree and naming helpers.
- `plainLabel(text, element)` → `{ label, badge }` or null: whether an element of a header or drawer `<nav>` is a link-less label the nav draws as an item (static words of its own, the words of an element nested in it as the chip `badge`; `readItems` skips one whose label or chip says it is coming soon, `isSoonEntry`); a control, a heading, a hidden element, bound text, a separator and anything holding a link or control is none. `readItems` gives such an item `targets: []`, `disabled: true` and the `badge`.
- `isChoiceFlow(node, isFilter?)` → whether an element is a choice flow: two or more pick lists that are no filter (`isFilter(list)`, the shared `narrowsRenderedList` rule) and no `<form>`.

### `lib/intake-pagemap-mega-slots.mjs`
- `megaSlots({ menu, openers, anchorOf, inside, itemOf, newMenu })` → Map(opener → `{ menu, position }`): inserts each opener the header menu lacks that sits inside the menu's element (`inside(opener)`) at its document place (`itemOf`), makes a menu with `newMenu()` when the header has none, and puts the openers outside the menu's element (and so outside its bar: the bar's far-side openers are already its items) into one second menu from a second `newMenu()`; renumbers the items; a null opener (a panel with no single opener) gets no slot.

### `lib/intake-pagemap-split.mjs`
- `splitLinks({ nav, header, routed, isNavigation, panels })` → `{ bar, logo, first, links }` or null: the navigation elements on the logo's far side from the header's nav, and which half comes first (`'nav'` or `'links'`).
- `placeSplit(menu, made, first)` → the menu with `made` added after (or before) its items, renumbered.
- `splitPoint(items)` → `{ position, label }` of the last item of the first half, or null when the items hold no split item or split items on both sides.

### `lib/skeleton-split-menu.mjs`
- `splitMenuOf(menuItems)` → `{ menu, after, labels, first }` or null; `splitLinkOf({ e, els, byKey, split, surfaceKind })` → `{ key, first, group }` or null; `sidesOf(split)` → `{ nav, links }` (`splitSide` values); `splitSlots({ at, link, finder, settings, calibrated })` → `{ slots, notes }`.

### `lib/site-build-menus-step.mjs`
- `supersededItems(rows, state, linkText?, surfaces?)` → `item-delete` actions; `menusStep(plan, superseded?)` → `{ actions, options, unresolved }`; `menuProblems(plan)` → the problems that stop the menus step (`problemsByStep.map` and `.menus`; every problem of a plan with no `problemsByStep`); `runMenus({ planFor, apply, wp, applyPhase, log?, error? })` → exit code.

### `lib/intake-spec-sync.mjs`
- `SPEC_FILE`, `DATA_DIR`: the spec and the route's `data/` folder. `LABELS`: each Appendix C label with its schema file and shape (`body`, or `items` for the page-map array).
- `specBlock(specText, label)` → the parsed JSON block after `**<label>:**`; throws naming the label when there is none.
- `constructKinds(specText)` → the construct kinds Appendix C lists for the registry.
- `syncProblems(specText, label, schema)` → each disagreement between the spec block and the schema file (wrapper keys ignored), prefixed with the label.
- `intakeProblems(specText, schema)` → each intake-record key missing from the schema's `required` or `properties`, and each extra required key.

### `lib/motion-schema.mjs`
- `REPO`, `MOTION_SCHEMA_FILE`: the repo root and the schema path. `loadMotionSchema(file?)` → the parsed schema. `annotationKeywords(schema)` → every `x-sgs-*` keyword the schema uses (registered with ajv).
- `RANGE_UNITS`, `RELATIVE_UNITS`: the base-unit conversions (ms/s, px, deg/turn/rad) and the units a ranged field refuses. `rangeProblem(range, value)` → the error text for a value outside an `x-sgs-range`, or null (tokens and `calc()` are not range-checked).
- `motionValidator(schema?)` → the compiled ajv validator (cached per schema). `formatError(e)` → one ajv error as `path: message`. `schemaErrors(doc, schema?)` → every schema error. `checkMotion(doc, schema?)` → `{ valid, errors, refusals }`.
- `enumerateFields(schema?)` → every field with its `x-sgs-field` annotation (panel, field type, CSS property, state, per-device), the list the DB motion-field rows are seeded from. Re-exports `motionRefusals`, `elementRefusals` and `elementLayers`.

### `lib/motion-validate.mjs`
- `SELECTOR_MAX_LENGTH`, `SELECTOR_ALLOWED`, `SELECTOR_DENIED`; `selectorProblem(selector)` → the reason a custom-target selector is not scoped to the block root, or null.
- `customTargetErrors(doc)` → the custom-target rule failures; `validateMotionWrite(doc, schema)` → `{ valid, errors, refusals }` (the schema's errors and refusals plus the custom-target errors); `assertMotionWritable(doc, schema)` throws one Error listing every problem and returns the document when it is writable.
- `verdictProblems(verdict)` → every problem of a verdict as text: its errors, then each refusal's text (a refusal is a string or `{ id, text, layers }`); `lib/fill-motion.mjs::writeNode`, `lib/fill-behaviour.mjs` and `assertMotionWritable` print it.

### `lib/motion-refusals.mjs`
- `elementLayers(element)` → `[{ list, path, effect, layer }]` in paint order. `layerLabel(schema, entry)` → the layer's display label. `slotClaims(schema, entry)` → the paint slots a layer claims. `matchedValues(entry, m)` → the rule side's value paths this layer sets (in values or a device override; with `nonZero`, a zero amount is unset). `sideLabel(schema, entry, m)` → the label a refusal names the layer by for that side (a `valueLabels` label when every matched value maps to one). `matches(schema, entry, m)` → whether a layer meets one side of a refusal rule.
- `elementRefusals(schema, element)` → the refusal texts for one element. `motionRefusals(schema, doc)` → `{ <target>: [texts] }` for every element of a document.

### `handoff-repackage.mjs`
- `parseArgs(argv)` → `{ folder, project, entries, generated, dryRun }` or `{ error }`. `main(argv, log?)` → the exit code.
- `readOldManifest(text)` → `{ rows: [{ path, bytes, sha256 }], runtime }` from an old `MANIFEST.md`.
- `proveUnchanged(root)` → `{ problems, notes }`: a problem is a file changed since export or a folder that cannot be proven unchanged.
- `repackage(root, { project, entries, generated, dryRun?, schemas? })` → `{ problems, notes, actions }`; writes nothing when `problems` is non-empty or `dryRun` is set.

### `lint.mjs`
- `routeFiles(root)` → every route file, relative.
- `exportsOf(src)` → exported names.
- `lintFolder(root)` → problems (README index, scripts imports, a file naming the plugin's `node_modules`).
- `lintTree(tree, db, label?)` → problems (core style, native_wp).
- `lintSkeleton(tree, db, label?)` → problems (style values; and a brand `sgs/icon` that types its own brand's address in `linkUrl` with no `metadata.bindings.linkUrl`).
- `registerIds(markdown)` → the item ids a fix register holds (table first cells, comma-split, and ids leading a bullet).
- `HOUSE_RULES`: ledger rules that are house rules (`touch-target`, `accessibility`): their entries cite no register item.
- `lintLedger(entries, ids, label?)` → problems: an entry (not a house rule) whose `register` ids are missing or not in `ids`.
- `lintSurfaceLedger(surfacesFile, registerFile?, repo?)` → `lintLedger` on `<build>/qa/divergences.json` against `registerFile`, else the register `qa/ledger.config.json` names (from the repo root); a ledger with entries and no register, or a missing register file, is a problem.

### `lib/fill-behaviour.mjs`
- `declaredAttr`: Whether the framework DB declares the attribute on the block (read-only). `db` is the handle the caller already holds (the default opens the framework DB once). A DB that cannot be read declares nothing: the write is refused, never assumed.
- `hasAttrOf`: The attribute check of a framework DB handle, the shape `hasAttr( block, attr )` the writers take.
- `behaviourIndex`: The recognised behaviours of the records, keyed for placement: those a record names by template element are found through `recordsByElement`; those a script finds by a `[data-*]` hook (no template element of their own) are held by the elements that carry the hook. Returns { hosted: [ { r, b } ], hostsOf(key) } where hostsOf gives the hosted ones for a template element key.
- `stripKeysOf`: The template elements that scroll away above a pinned header: when the draft pins one element (a sticky header that also shadows on scroll), its earlier siblings that are not pinned themselves scroll off the page while the bar stays, as do their descendants. A Set of template keys.
- `templateOf`: A fact record's template in the shape `behaviourIndex` reads: `{ elements, scrolled }`, `scrolled` the looks the draft's scrolled state gives each element.
- `applySettings`: Writes a node's block settings from its settings behaviours (the behaviours whose block declares each attribute, a framework DB query); `colour` values equal to a palette colour are written by their slug. A behaviour no settings of this node's block belong to is reported. Returns the items it wrote or reported.
- `applyStrip`: The header row that scrolls away above the pinned header bar: `rowHideOnScroll` on a `sgs/site-header-row` whose element is one of the strip keys, and `rowAnimate` off where the block declares it and `stillAtRest` holds.
- `stillAtRest`: The resting transition-duration of a target at every width it renders at (the code's declaration, else the rendered value) when every entry is 0 and no state look in `reads.states` declares or renders a non-zero transition or animation duration; a width the finder found nothing visible at is skipped, while an unread width, a failed declared read or no rendering width gives null.
- `place`: Puts a finished layer into the document where writeEffect placed it. An element's effect list holds each effect once (the motion schema's unique-effect limit), so a layer whose effect the list already holds is not added: the layer already there stands, and the return names it with the fields where the second layer differs ({ placed: false, layer, differs }); otherwise { placed: true, layer }. `lib/fill-motion.mjs::motionWrites` and `applyBehaviours` both place through it.
- `sharedLayerRow`: The row or note for a layer `place` did not add: the same values are one layer shared by both records (a note); different values are a named row, because the element holds the effect once and the first record's values stand.
- `applyBehaviours`: One node target's behaviours. `items`: [ { r, b } ]; `finish( effect, id )` writes and checks one effect (writeEffect, preset, token snapping); `written` maps a record id to where its layer went (a control's target); `controls` collects the controls for the second pass. Pushes to out.writes, out.unmapped, out.notes and out.site.
- `applyGlobals`: The behaviours that belong to no element: the draft's route fade (a site option) and the ones SGS already does (a scroll reset on a route change, the page scroll lock of a modal drawer, a back-to-top press). Each is reported once.
- `draftCssOf`: The draft's CSS text for the pointer-tracked reveal's consumer check: the draft file(s), which hold their styles inline (`style` attributes and `<style>` blocks). [] when the draft is served from a URL.
- `applyControls`: The second pass: each control sets values on the layer of the record it controls (the marquee's hover rate). The merged layer is validated on its own before it is kept, so a control value the schema refuses names the control instead of failing the whole node's document; the row carries the controlled record's node (where its layer, or its own row, sits).

### `lib/fill-current-item.mjs`
- `CURRENT_PATH`: The loop variable's property names a draft uses for "this item is the current route".
- `currentItemGroups`: The current-item groups of a fact record: [{ ifKey, itemKey, markKey, component, itemN, markN, path }]. Only an sc-if inside an sc-for, whose single hole is a current-like path, answered both true and false across the loop, with an element child.
- `groupOfJob`: The group a read job (a target with a `{ tpl: '<chain>/<n>#<copy>' }` finder) is the item of, or undefined.
- `currentSelectors`: The two selectors of a group: the copy where the condition holds and a copy where it does not.
- `readCurrentItems`: Reads the current-item looks at the page's current width: { looks: { [jobId]: [look] }, gaps: [{ ids, reason }] }. groups: currentItemGroups(facts); jobs: lib/fill-read.mjs::jobsFor. The comparison copy is read here, so the look is the current copy against a non-current copy of the same item, never against a target that may itself be the current copy.


### `lib/fill-current-attr.mjs`
- `currentAttrKeys( facts )`: the template keys of the elements whose `aria-current` the draft binds to a value (a header component writing `aria-current="{{ cur.shop }}"` on each nav link, with no sc-if and no selector).
- `currentAttrJobs( keys, jobs, rootComponent )`: the read jobs that are one of those elements, each with its component, its tpl and `bound` (the tpls of every element of that component whose `aria-current` the draft binds: the only elements it may pair with, so loop copies and the bar's other bound links are peers and a lone link in a box beside the nav is not); a job inside the page's own root component is dropped.
- `readCurrentAttr( { jobs, pages, openSibling, resolveSrc, log } )`: opens the draft's other pages at the read width, and where a peer of the item carries `aria-current` the peer's declared values against a non-current peer's are the item's `current` look (`states: ['current']`, written by `fillStates`); a job no page answers is one gap row. Spec 48 FR-48-81.

### `lib/fill-state-parts.mjs`
- `partStateSlots( { db, cal, block, prop, slot, state } )`: the slots a state setting was measured at on another instance of a repeated part (`canonical_slot` or `css_element` names the part, a `::before` or `::after` layer counting as the element), for a state look the draft shows on an instance the setting was not measured on. `lib/fill-state.mjs::fillStates` adds them to the slots it tries.

### `lib/setting-variant.mjs`
- `rowHoldsVariant( comps, part, element )`: whether one record row's selector carries `--<element>` on an element compound above its part (`.x__item--featured .x__link`), the modifier not sitting on the part's own element.
- `variantOnlyOf( rows, element, compoundsOf )`: the variant (the setting's `css_element`) a setting is limited to, or null; `setting-record.mjs::settingEntry` stamps it as the entry's `variantOnly`. `current` is a state, never a variant.
- `variantHeld( entry, variants )`: whether a node drawn in `variants` (`node.drawnVariants`, `featured`) may take the entry; `lib/resolve.mjs::resolve` applies it when it ties a setting to an element.

### `lib/resolve-layer.mjs`
- `coversSlot( c, p, slot, prop )`: whether record path `p` of setting entry `c` is a `::before` or `::after` cover layer (its `inset` among the entry's effects) over the element at `slot`, for a draft background; `resolve` tries such a setting when no setting paints the element itself (`itemBgHover` for a plain link's hover fill).

### `lib/fill-scrim.mjs`
- `backdropLook( facts )`: the draft's backdrop beside its drawers (the fact record's surface part of kind `backdrop`) as an opaque colour, the strength (the rgba alpha times any opacity it declares), a blur radius and the opacity fade in ms.
- `scrimWrites( { nodes, flat, refOf, facts, scrimBlocks, defaultOf } )`: writes `scrimColour`, `scrimOpacity`, `scrimBlur` and `scrimFadeDuration` on every node of a block whose settings paint a scrim (`css_element = 'scrim'`: `sgs/nav-drawer`, `sgs/cart`), skipping a default and a value the node already holds. Spec 48 FR-48-8.
### `lib/fill-form-schema.mjs`
- `formSchemaOf`: The form schema the fact record holds for a component: { component, entry, steps } or null. A component whose statics hold no array of steps with named fields has none.
- `schemaFieldOf`: The schema field a rendered control is: its id or name ends with the field's name (`ta-tradingName` is `tradingName`).
- `schemaChipsOf`: The schema field a group of choice chips is: the choice field whose options are exactly the chips' labels.
- `conditionsFromSource`: The conditions in a component's script: { <field name>: { field, op, value } \| { reason } }. The script's tests are read as `const x = ['a', 'b'].includes(v.f)` (an either-or list), `const x = v.f === 'a'` (equals) and `const x = v.f === false` (an unticked box); a field's `show: x` (or `show: !x`) names the test it waits on. One value is a condition the form blocks hold (`conditionalField`, `conditionalOperator`, `conditionalValue`); a list is not.
- `linkParams`: The query-string names the draft's links hand to a page (`?team=Sales&role=Driver`): every `href` in the fact record's templates, static or a hole's literal part.
- `savesProgress`: Whether the draft keeps a form's answers in the browser: the intake flags (lib/intake-flags.mjs) name a `localStorage` write in the component's logic.
- `requiredCopyOf`: The validation copy in a component's script, read from its syntax: per-field `if (!v.name) errs.name = '…'` lines and the shared per-type `f.req` line. Returns { fields: { <name>: { required?, tooLong? } }, byType }.
- `copyFor`: The copy one rendered control shows: { required?, tooLong? }; a schema field the draft does not require gets none.
- `schemaFieldByName`: The schema field whose name is `name`: { field, step }, or null when no field of the schema has that name.

### `lib/fill-form.mjs`
- `isFormFieldBlock(slug)` → whether a block is a form field (`sgs/form-field-*`), the blocks `formFieldWrites` fills.
- `attrDef`: The attribute definition of a block by framework-DB query: { default } or null when the block holds no such attribute.
- `formFieldWrites`: The writes, UNMAPPED rows and notes for one field block. block: its slug; attributes: what the node holds; el: the draft control's `snap.form`; field: the schema field it is ({ field, step }) or null; param: the link parameter names of the draft; condition: { field, op, value } \| { reason } \| null.
- `formReadback`: Reads a written value back against the draft fact it came from; returns the problems (empty when they agree).
- `formWrites`: Fill's form pass. nodes/flat/refOf: the skeleton nodes, their tree nodes and the ref function; reads: readDraft's result; facts: the fact record (or null); flags: intake's flags; db: the framework DB; source: { component: script text } for the draft's conditions ({ component: script text }, see formSources); component: the surface's own component, whose schema is used (none named reads the first schema in the record); idxFor( component ): the parsed logic of a draft component (`lib/fill-list-content.mjs::logicReader`), from which a multi-step form's button words are read (`lib/fill-form-buttons.mjs`); buttonRules: `rules.formSteps` (read from the decisions file when omitted). A linked reference block (`formIsLinked`) and the blocks inside it are never written. Returns { writes, unmapped, notes, settled }: `settled` is one row (reason `row-held`, property `(linked form)`) for each node on or inside a linked reference block that the draft read, naming the linked form.
- `componentOf`: The component whose template a control comes from: the innermost import in the chain of its `tpl` finder that is one of the candidates (the script that validates it), or null when the finder names no template.
- `formSources`: The scripts of the draft's components that hold a form schema or required-field copy: { component: text } read from `<folder>/<component>.dc.html`; a named `component` reads that component's schema's script, none the first schema's.
- `schemaControl`: The control a schema field stands for when the page never rendered it, in the shape of the draft read's `snap.form`: its name, its autocomplete token and its options as the block takes them (choices for a block holding `tiles`, else options whose value and label are the draft's option).

### `lib/fill-form-buttons.mjs`
FR-48-57: the words of a multi-step form's own buttons. The draft's Next and Back buttons the skeleton absorbed (the form component's buttons outside any loop that `navRole` names) give the `sgs/form` node's `nextLabel`, `submitLabel` and `prevLabel`; `formWrites` calls it on a form node that holds `sgs/form-step` children.
- `stepRules`: `rules.formSteps` of `data/skeleton-decisions.json`.
- `trueOnLast`: Whether a test holds on the last step: true or false for a comparison with `<list>.length - 1` (`===`, `==`, `>=`, `<=`, `<`, `>`, `!==`, `!=`, either way round, through names and `!`), else null.
- `holeWords`: The words one hole path shows, followed through the object `renderVals` returns: `{ plain }`, `{ rest, last }` (a value chosen by a step test: the last step's and the others') or `{ reason }`.
- `buttonWords`: The words one button shows: its own text, or the one text hole the fact record reads as a string (an element hole, an icon, is no words); static text beside a hole, several holes or an unread hole is a `{ reason }`; no words is null.
- `stepButtonLabels`: `{ labels, notes }`: the Next button's words give `nextLabel` (and `submitLabel` from its last-step words), the Back button's one set of words `prevLabel`; copies that disagree, unreadable words and a Back button that changes words by step write nothing and are notes.
- `stepButtonWrites`: The writes for the form node: each label that differs from what the node reads as now (its value, else the block default); a label the block holds no setting for is a named UNMAPPED row.

### `lib/fill-list-marker.mjs`
- `iconItems(db, block)` → `{ attr, fields, roles }`, the block's item array whose item schema holds an icon setting the icon reader writes (and each field's declared role), or null.
- `markerPart(settings)` → the recorded marker part as the first copy's slot (the shortest slot under a repeated step, not a pseudo-element, whose `<slot> > svg` the setting record also names), or null.
- `markerSlotAt(part, k)` → the part's slot for item copy `k` (its last repeated step set to `k`).
- `itemSlotAt(part, k)` → the item part of copy `k` (the marker part cut after its last repeated step), or null.
- `markerSlots({ cal, slots, reads })` → `{ <copy number>: slot }`, each item copy's marker slot among the node's measured slots: its marker part, else `<item slot>::marker` where `reads` shows the item's own element drawing a CSS marker.
- `ordinal(words)` → `{ n, formats }` for a typed ordinal (`1`, `01`, `1.`, `(1)`, `i.`, `a)`), else null; `glyph(text)` → `{ kind: 'numbered' | 'bullet' | 'emoji', ... }`; `drawnByPart(read)` and `drawnByCss(read)` → what a marker part's read, or an item's CSS (list-style type, `::marker` content, `::before` counter, glyph or small painted dot), draws.
- `markerSettingsFrom(rows)` → `{ marker, number }`, the enum settings of a block that hold the marker kinds and the number styles (`MARKERS` is the kinds).
- `listMarkerDecisions({ db, block, cal, attributes, reads })` → `{ writes, unmapped, notes, decided? }`.

### `lib/fill-icon.mjs`
- `ICON_SETTINGS` → the settings `iconDecisions` can write: `iconSource`, `brandName`, `iconName`, `iconSvg`, `iconFill`, `iconPosition`.
- `iconSettings(schema)` → those of them the block declares, or `[]` for a block with no `iconSvg`; the guard `iconDecisions` writes by.
- `KSES_FILE`: the plugin's `includes/helpers-svg-kses.php`, whose allowlist the writer parses.
- `LUCIDE_FILE`: the plugin's `includes/lucide-icons.php`, the Lucide glyphs a stroke mark is matched against.
- `BRAND_FILE`: the plugin's `data/brand-registry.json`, the brand glyphs a mark is matched against.
- `allowedSvg(file)` → the sanitiser's allowed tags and attributes `{ tag: Set(attribute) }`, parsed from the PHP source so the writer keeps exactly what the page keeps.
- `keptSvg(markup, allowed?)` → draft SVG markup as the icon's sanitiser keeps it (tags and attributes allowed, class, style and a root width and height dropped), or null when nothing drawable is left; the marquee items rule writes item icons through it.
- `statedSvgSize(markup)` → the size in pixels a draft SVG states on its root (`width` and `height` equal, plain pixels or none), or null; `keptSvg` drops that size, so `rules.headerStripBar` reads it first and decides the bar's `iconBareSize` from it (`style.iconSize` in `data/skeleton-decisions.json`), only when every label states the same size.
- `signature`: The shape signature of a mark: each drawing element's tag and geometry, so the same drawing matches however it is painted.
- `lucideSignatures`: { signature: icon name } for every Lucide icon the block ships, read from includes/lucide-icons.php.
- `lucideNearest(markup, tolerance = 1, file?)` → the Lucide icon a hand-drawn mark copies: the one icon whose every drawing element has a counterpart in the mark (same tag, same geometry attributes and path commands, every number within `tolerance`, in any order of drawing), or null when none does or two different icons are equally close. The skeleton's `rules.formControl.fieldIcon` reads a field's mark through it.
- `brandSignatures`: { signature: brand slug } for each registry brand whose glyph is its own SVG, and { slug: signature } the other way round.
- `markKind`: The kind of mark: 'stroke' (every drawing element is stroked and unfilled), 'filled' (none is stroked, every one is filled) or 'mixed'; and whether it is drawn the way Lucide draws (stroke width 2, round caps and joins).
- `iconDecisions`: svg: the element's read ({ markup, position }) or null. schema: the block's settings. attributes: what the node already holds. href: the address the mark links to in the draft (or ''), the evidence a Site Info brand row is that brand.

### `lib/fill-logo-size.mjs`
- `logoSizeSettings`: { width, max, unit } setting names a block has for a logo's size, or null.
- `logoSizeWrites({ nodes, flat, refOf, reads, db, unmapped })` → `{ writes, unmapped, notes }`: a logo whose one width setting cannot hold the draft's per-width sizes (the coded gap row) is written as its per-device size setting instead.

### `lib/fill-dimensions.mjs`
- `SIZE_FAMILY`: the size properties (height, width, min-*, max-*) with their kind (exact, min, max) and axis; the logical forms (block-size, inline-size) map onto them.
- `physical`: the physical name of a size property (`min-block-size` is `min-height`).
- `sizeOf`: { kind, axis } of a size property, or null.
- `MIN_TARGET`: 24: the px an interactive element's written height or width never goes below (WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8).
- `calibratedAt(cal, slot, prop)` → whether a resting setting painting `prop` is recorded on `slot` of the block. Rule 2b of `dimensionWrites`: a declared height or width on a replaced image (img, picture, video, canvas) whose other dimension is not declared as a length goes to the block's `max-height` or `max-width` setting recorded on that element, when the block paints the element larger at every width (the ceiling clamps it to the declared size and the other dimension follows); it is asked on the element itself, never on the root it may be the content box of.
- `innerImageSlot(cal)` → the block's one inner image element (its site-look default paint's `_tag` img), or null when it has none or several. Rule 2b asks a picture read at the block's root (an `<img>`, `<picture>`, `<video>`, `<canvas>` or a custom element drawing one) on that slot's ceiling, and reads a fluid declared size (clamp(), min(), max(), calc()) as the rendered size at that width.
- `dimensionWrites({ nodes, flat, refOf, reads, db, unmapped, calFor, snapshot, scope, entries, date })` → `{ writes, unmapped, notes, ledger }`: a block's floor or ceiling the draft does not declare is written at the draft's rendered size, a declared size in a dimension with no setting goes to the block's minimum when the content fits (else the row stays with the reason), and an interactive size under 24px is written as 24px with a `touch-target` ledger entry.
- `contentExtent({ nodes, reads }, rec, target, axis, w)` → the content extent inside an element along an axis at a width, or null. `NATURAL_SIZE`: the child width (`auto`) that holds a non-shrinking item at its natural size under `fixed` child sizing.

### `lib/fill-layer-rotation.mjs`
- `layerRotationWrites({ nodes, flat, refOf, reads, db, unmapped, motionWrites })` → `{ writes, unmapped, answered }`: the pass after the motion pass that writes a decorative layer's computed turn (`transform` read as a pure-rotation matrix) to the layer's `rotation` setting in degrees (the setting the database ties to `transform` on the wrapper), `how` `layer-rotation`, settled reason `layer-rotation`. A layer whose written sgsMotion holds a resting pose (`restRotate`) is left to it (writing both would turn the layer twice), and a matrix with a pixel offset, scale or skew stays raised.

### `lib/fill-regap.mjs`
- `TIER_OF`: the tier name of each read width.
- `rowTarget`: the skeleton node and target an unmapped row names, or null.
- `rowValues`: a row's per-width values; a width the row omits takes the draft's rendered value there. A row of one mode's widths (`modeWidths`, `lib/fill-device-mode.mjs`) holds those widths only.
- `rectAt`: the draft's rendered box of a target at a width, or null.
- `reresolve`: runs the generic resolver (lib/fill-prop.mjs::resolveProperty) on a changed per-width draft for a gap row's element, with no baseline.
- `commit`: writes a resolver result into the node and records each write.
- `perNode(rows)`: a row UNMAPPED raises once for several nodes (`nodes`, `lib/fill-row-lift.mjs::liftChildren`) as one row per node, so a pass reads and writes each node it names.
- `regroup(rows)`: joins the rows a pass leaves back into one row per look and reason.

### `lib/fill-map.mjs`
- `zoomOf`: The zoom a Google Maps embed address asks for (`z=15`, or `zoom=15`), a whole number from 1 to 20; null when it names none.
- `mapDecisions`: embeds: { width: { src, filter, h } } the iframe the draft paints at each read width (lib/fill-read.mjs `embed`; a width the element is not shown at is absent). schema: the block's settings. attributes: what the node already holds.

### `lib/fill-motion-account.mjs`
- `accountedIds`: The record ids a finished run has already accounted for: the layers it wrote (`used`), the layers a control or behaviour placed (`written`), and every record id an UNMAPPED row, a note (`<id>: ...`), a write's property or a site option names.
- `makeHomeOf`: Where a record sits on the surface: `homeOf( record )` is { n (the skeleton node), slot } or null for a record whose element is not a target; `homeOf.within( record )` is the nearest target above its element in `template` (`parentChain`), for an element this surface dropped or absorbed. nodes: skeletonNodes(); keyOf( finder ): the inventory key of a target's element; idx: lib/fill-behaviour.mjs::behaviourIndex; template: lib/fill-behaviour.mjs::templateOf.
- `styleSourceIds({ written, records })` → the ids of the style records the written effects read their created element's declarations from: the effect holds them, so they count as accounted.
- `silentRows`: The UNMAPPED rows for the on-surface records nothing accounted for (see makeHomeOf), at the nearest target above an element this surface dropped (`homeOf.within`); a record under no target belongs to another surface; refOf( node ): the node's ref.
- `READING_PROGRESS_SETTING`: The page's reading progress bar: a record the effect recogniser reads as a page-scroll progress bar whose element is not on the surface (the skeleton removes the thin fixed bar: rules.readingProgress). Nothing in the tree can hold it; the Floating UI reading progress setting does, so the handover names the setting and the record for site build.
- `readingProgressHandover({ found, homeOf })` → a handover row naming `READING_PROGRESS_SETTING` for each page scroll-progress record no surface holds.
- `motionWidths(n, doc, reads)` → the read widths a node's sgsMotion write answers: the widths its root element was read at, where the document gives the root a layer state of its own, else none.

### `lib/fill-preset.mjs`
- `PRESET_KEYS`: the looks compared against a button preset variant: `[ key, css properties, state ]` per row.
- `presetBlocks`: The block settings that hold a preset variant, by framework-DB query: { block: attr } for every block with an `inheritStyle` setting whose values include the preset slugs.
- `matchPreset`: The preset variant a target matches at every read width, or null. presets: settings.custom.buttonPresets.
- `presetWrites`: Writes the matched variant onto every preset block whose draft element matches, and drops the per-instance values the resolver wrote for the properties the variant sets. nodes: skeletonNodes(); flat: tree nodes by index; refOf: tree node to ref; reads: readDraft's result; rawSnapshot/snapshot: the client's theme snapshot (raw, normalised); writes: Fill's writes. Returns { writes (the list without the dropped ones, plus the variant writes), notes }.
- `TRANSFORM_CHANNELS`: the hover-state fields that paint the CSS `transform`. `presetVariants(db, presets)` → `{ block: { attr, variants } }` for every block with an `inheritStyle` setting, an enum setting holds the snapshot's preset names the enum includes, a string setting with no enum is open and holds every snapshot name except `RESERVED_STYLES` (`default`, `link`, `custom`). `matchNamed({ preset, variant, reads, id, snapshot })` → the preset a draft mount names, matched key by key (the properties whose value equals the draft's, rest and hover apart). `presetWrites` also takes `mounts` (`lib/fill-mount-version.mjs::mountVersions`): a node mounted with a version the snapshot carries takes that preset before any look is matched, a version it does not carry is noted and left unwritten. `dropPresetMotion({ lifted, flat, writes })` → removes the hover transform channels from the per-instance motion of every node whose painted preset variant holds the draft's hover transform, so the preset is the one writer of the lift.

### `lib/fill-mount-version.mjs`
- `versionDefaults(folder)` → `{ Component: default version or null }` for every component file of a draft folder that declares an enum prop `version`.
- `mountVersions({ nodes, facts, rootComponent, defaults })` → `Map(node index → { version, component, how })`: the preset a draft mount names (Spec 48A FR-48A-17) for each skeleton node whose draft element is the control (`a` or `button`) of a versioned component mount, read from the mount's fact record (`version="gold"`, or the component's declared default); a bound version (`{{ }}`) is not read.

### `lib/fill-safe-area.mjs`
- `safeAreaSides`: The sides a declaration asks the safe-area inset for.
- `fixedPart`: The value of a declaration with every safe-area inset taken as 0px, when it is a sum or a maximum of px terms (`calc(16px + env(...))`, `max(16px, env(...))`, `env(...)` alone); null for a form it does not evaluate.
- `safeAreaRead`: declared: the draft's declared text for one property; rendered: what the draft paints (a px length).

### `lib/fill-scrollbar.mjs`
- `splitScrollbarColour`: A computed `scrollbar-color` ("rgba(231, 215, 104, 0.75) rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)") as { thumb, track } colours, or null for `auto`.
- `isDark`: Whether a ground colour is dark (relative luminance under 0.4); a transparent ground is not a ground.
- `scrollbarTokens`: items: [{ from: { node, block, slot, index }, color, width, ground, thumbPart, trackPart }] read from the draft's scrollers. snapshot: lib/normalise.mjs::loadSnapshot. site: the client's current settings.custom.scrollbar (or undefined).
- `scrollbarPatch`: The scrollbar tokens of a whole surface: the scrollers read at the widest width, once each, as a patch of the client's theme-snapshot.json. Returns { patch, entries, notes, unmapped }.
- `mergePatch`: Two snapshot patches as one (the keys are disjoint paths of the same object).

### `lib/fill-state-defect.mjs`
- `droppedStateDecls`: The defect rows of intake's `draftDefects` (groups hold `rows`) that name a dropped state declaration: [{ draftId, pseudo, prop, declared }].
- `holeValue`: The single string a hole resolved to at one width for one copy of its element, or { gap }. `answer` is the fact record's `{ v: [ summary ], n, loop }`; a loop's list holds one summary per copy, in order.
- `addDefectLooks`: Adds the code looks of every dropped declaration to `reads.states[width].looks[jobId]` (in place) and returns { listed, gaps }. reads: lib/fill-read.mjs::readDraft's result; jobs: [{ id, finder }]; facts: the fact record; draftDefects: intake.json's; rootComponent: the entry draft's component (lib/fill-confirm.mjs::draftIdOf). A look already read for the same state and property at a width (the page did paint it) is kept as read.

### `lib/draft-defects.mjs`
- `OWNER_DEFAULT`, `FIELDS` (every field an entry holds); `defectRows(draftDefects)` → the defect rows of intake's `draftDefects`; `defectKey(row)` → the key a defect keeps across re-runs.
- `catalogueDefects(catalogue, { owner, date })` → one entry per `draft-omission` gap row of a catalogue (a choice the product page offers that the basket line never reads).
- `buildDraftDefects({ draftDefects, listed, owner, date })` → the list entries for one intake, `listed` being Fill's `addDefectLooks` rows (what the code intent was built as); `mergeDraftDefects(fresh, earlier)` → the list a re-run writes, each entry keeping the dates and owner of the earlier one; `validateDraftDefects(list)` → why a list is invalid, as strings.

### `lib/draft-defects-file.mjs`
- `defectsPath(client, repo)` → the file path; `draftDefectsFile({ client, repo, owner, listed, date })` → `{ client, takenOn, defects }`; `writeDraftDefects(file, { client, repo })`.
- `requestText(file)` → the request text for entries not yet sent, grouped by owner; `markSent(file, date)` → the file with `date` stamped on every entry that has no sent date.

### `lib/fill-width-gate.mjs`
- `TIERS`: the device tier boundaries, 768 and 1024.
- `SNAP_TOLERANCE`: 5%: a width threshold this close to a tier snaps to it, with a `breakpoint-snap` ledger entry.
- `HIDE_ATTR`: the conditional-visibility settings per tier (`sgsHideOnMobile`, `sgsHideOnTablet`, `sgsHideOnDesktop`); each is checked against the block in the framework DB before it is written.
- `TIER_RANGES`: The width range each tier covers: [ start, end ).
- `holds`: Whether a width condition holds (shows its content) at width `w`.
- `shownRanges`: The ranges [ lo, hi ) of widths from 0 at which a condition shows its content, merged.
- `intersect`: The overlap of two lists of ranges.
- `complement`: The complement of a list of ranges within [ 0, Infinity ).
- `snapThreshold`: FR-48-50 step 1: the tier a threshold snaps to, with its distance in px, or null (no tier within 5% of the tier, or the threshold is the tier). The nearest tier wins.
- `shownAt`: The widths a template element is shown at, from the width conditions of its enclosing sc-ifs: { shown, via } or null when no enclosing sc-if is gated by width.
- `hiddenRanges`: The snapped hidden ranges of a shown list: { hidden: [ [ lo, hi ] ], snaps: [ { draft, tier, distance } ] }.
- `mediaRule`: The scoped @media rule hiding a range (width in whole px; the rule `&` is the instance, includes/custom-css.php).
- `collapseAttributes`: The setting each block draws its own alternative below (the nav's burger under its collapse point), as the skeleton rules name it: data/skeleton-decisions.json `rules.navigation.collapseAttribute`, { block: attr }.
- `ownBreakpoint`: The numeric collapse setting a block holds, by framework-DB query: the attribute the skeleton rules name for the block, when the block holds it as a number; null for any other block, whatever other breakpoint-like numbers it holds.
- `tierRanges`: the width ranges of the tiers a list of read widths (375, 768, 1440) stands for, merged.
- `maskHiddenVariants`: a width-variant instance's reads at the widths it is hidden at become missing, before any pass, so two instances measured on one draft element never stand side by side as two children. `shownOfNode`: the widths a skeleton node's content is shown at: its enclosing sc-if's range, or for a width-variant instance (`widthShown` on the variant, `widthVariants` on the default instance) the range of its own element, the default instance being shown where no variant is.
- `scopedCssPuts`: the `sgsCustomCss`, scope key and label writes that append a scoped rule to a node; empty when the node holds the rule already. The one writer of a scoped rule.
- `scopeKeyOf(node, fallback)`: the node's scope key (`sgsCustomCssId`), a hash of its own ref (`cr-ref-<surface>-<n>`) in the 4 to 16 lowercase letters and digits `includes/custom-css.php::sgs_custom_css_uid` accepts, so the header's, footer's, drawer's and page's nodes drawn on one page never share a class; a node with no ref keeps `fallback`. `lib/fill-motion.mjs` keys a loop's CSS the same way.
- `snapEntry`: the `breakpoint-snap` ledger entry of one snapped threshold, numbered after the entries held.
- `desktopOnlyPin(pin)`: a pin setting trimmed to the desktop tier (`tablet` and `mobile` `none`), or null when it holds none or is already so. `presenceStep(reads, nodes, index)`: the pair of swept widths a node (or the nearest ancestor with one step) goes from not rendered to rendered between. `draftThresholds(buildDir)`: the width thresholds the draft's code uses, from the client's intake. A skeleton node marked `ownAlternativeBelow` (the filter rail) gets no hide flag and no scoped rule; `ownAlternativeBelow.value` is the draft's threshold in px, never snapped (an sc-if's own edge, else the one intake threshold inside the sweep's presence step), absent with an UNMAPPED row when neither names one; its `pinEdge` is desktop only.
- `widthGateWrites`: Writes the width gates of every skeleton node. nodes: skeletonNodes(); flat: tree nodes by index; refOf: tree node to ref; facts: the fact record (null: nothing written); db: the framework DB; scope: the surface; entries: the ledger's entries (the snap entries continue its numbering). Returns { writes, unmapped, notes, ledger } in the shapes lib/fill-resolve.mjs uses; `ledger` holds the new snap entries.
- `unite(a, b)` → the union of two lists of ranges. `placedChildWidening(nodes, facts, rootComponent)` → the width gate of every gated skeleton node as `Map( tree index -> { shown, via } )`, a wrapper's shown range widened to hold every block placed in it (the header and footer slot rows, `lib/skeleton-header-slots.mjs`), and a child that relied on the wrapper's gate keeping it.

### `lib/fill-reveal-marks.mjs`
- `REVEAL_MARKS`, `REVEAL_PRESET`, `isRevealed(data)`: the draft's scroll-reveal mark names (`data-reveal`) and the framework preset (`entrance-fade-up`, the client's `entrance` tokens) a marked element's block takes.
- `revealMarkWrites({ nodes, flat, refOf, inventory, mdb, schema })`: writes `sgsMotion` `elements.root.entrance.base` (preset, trigger `scroll`, the preset's token values) on every skeleton node whose draft element's inventory `data` carries a reveal mark and that holds no root entrance yet; validated by `validateMotionWrite`; a block with no motion target is an UNMAPPED row. An unmarked block gets none. Returns `{ writes, unmapped, notes }`. `tests/fill-reveal-marks.test.mjs`: MUST FAIL on the old Fill (nothing reads a mark); negatives: unmarked, another `data-` mark, no inventory, an existing entrance kept.

### `lib/fill-loop-copy.mjs`
- `copyClassSlot({ slot, target, prop, state, rec, cal, db, facts, rootComponent })` → the path a selector rule is written at: the part's class (the position removed) when it is a loop copy every copy shares, else `slot`.
- `paintsEveryCopy(cal, db, block, prop, state, slot)`: whether a recorded setting of the block that paints the property reaches the part on more than one copy.

### `lib/fill-width-ladder.mjs`
- `restingHeld({ widths, prop, state, base, hasSetting, raw })`: whether a one-value setting should hold the widest width's value of a property whose per-width values need `@media` rules: no state, a setting of the block paints it, the block's recorded paint (`base(w)`) is the property's initial value at every width, and the draft's widest value (`raw`) is not.
- `isLadderRow`: whether an unmapped row is a one-value-every-width gap, a value the setting's enum does not hold, a keyword a per-device setting cannot take, or a property whose setting paints another element of the block (never a size property).
- `effectOf`: what a value does in its element's context, as one canonical word (`normal` justify-content in a flex container is the start value; `space-between` with one visible child is too).
- `widthLadderWrites({ nodes, flat, refOf, reads, db, unmapped, calFor, snapshot, scope, entries, date, facts, rootComponent })` → `{ writes, unmapped, notes, ledger }`: a per-width difference no single setting holds is written as an equal-in-effect value, a tier-shaped sibling (a tie broken as the resolver breaks it, `lib/resolve.mjs::ownElementSetting`), the block's own breakpoint setting, or a scoped `@media` rule, in that order.
- `widthSpans({ widths, values, series })` → `{ ranges, snaps }`: the width ranges each read width's value holds over (the sweep's threshold, else the tier boundary, snapped to a tier within 5%), neighbours with one value merged; the ladder's rung 4 and `lib/fill-residual-css.mjs` share it. `safeCss(prop, slot, values)`: whether they can be written as safe CSS, by `SAFE_VALUE` and `SAFE_SLOT` (the characters a value and an element path may hold). `STATE_PSEUDO`: the pseudo-class of each state a rule can hold.
- `writtenTarget(rec, target, slot, notes)`: the skeleton target of the element the ladder writes: the row's own, or the node's target at that slot; with no target at that slot, the row's own and a note.
- `valuesAt(row, reads, target, home)`: the per-width values for the written element: the row's values when the row is on it or is a state row; otherwise that element's rendered values at the widths it is read at, never mixed with the row element's, keeping a row value declared in a form the computed read loses (`DECLARED_FORM`). A padding side read on the row's element, where the written element is another draft element inside it (a painted band around a width wrapper), is the sum of both paddings (px only).

### `lib/fill-step-rungs.mjs`
- `stepStretches(prop, series, tierValue)` → `[ { range: [lo, hi), value } ]`: the runs of the 16px sweep where the draft's value differs from the tier read that stands for that width (`tierValue('mobile' | 'tablet' | 'desktop')`) and touches a real step (a fluid ramp is not one).
- `stepRungWrites({ nodes, flat, refOf, reads, writes, scope, entries, date })` → `{ writes, notes, ledger }`: for every written per-device or single-value property whose sweep steps between the read widths, a scoped `@media` rule on the instance in Additional CSS at the draft's threshold (snapped to a tier within 5%, with a `breakpoint-snap` ledger entry); the nav item padding `w < 1200 ? 10px : 15px` is held from 1024 to 1199.
- `siblingSlot(slot)` → the slot with its sibling position (`:nth-of-type`) removed, so the copies of a repeated element share one key.

### `lib/loop-body.mjs`
- `loopKeyOf`: The innermost `sc-for` a template element sits in, or null.
- `staticAtEachWidth`: Whether a property gives one value across the loop's copies at each read width (the value may differ between widths): no style hole for it answers with more than one distinct value at any one width. `staticIn` is the stricter test across widths too.
- `staticIn`: Whether a property is the same in every copy of a template element: no style hole for it (or for a shorthand it belongs to) answers with more than one distinct value across the loop's copies.
- `loopBodyCheck`: The callback for the hop. facts: the fact record; identityOf( ancestor, path ) -> the template key (`<component>/<n>`) of the draft element behind a measured path, or null when the runtime names none (the origin map, lib/fill-skeleton.mjs::originMap).
- `identityFromOrigin`: identityOf for loopBodyCheck from the surface's origin map ({ [cr-ref]: { tpl } }, lib/fill-skeleton.mjs::originMap): the measured path of an ancestor came from the descendant ref the caller recorded in `ancestor.measuredRefs`.

### `lib/motion-behaviours.mjs`
- `withEnds`: A property that states its values only in its formula, as a choice between two literals (`cond ? 'a' : 'b'`, the shape intake's re-derived inventory writes), with `to` the first and `from` the second; a stated `from` or `to` is kept.
- `recogniseBehaviour(record, ctx)` → null for a record that is not a script-driven behaviour, else `{ kind: 'effect' | 'settings' | 'control' | 'site' | 'close' | 'native' | 'covered' | 'unmapped', … }` (the module header lists each shape); the record's formula-only values are filled first (`withEnds`).
- `effectRows`: The review rows of the `effect` row type (lib/intake-review.mjs): one per recognised behaviour a visitor or a reviewer confirms once, and one per behaviour no SGS effect expresses. `ctx` is recogniseBehaviour's.
- `hostsFromTemplate`: The attribute selector -> element keys map of a read template: every element whose attributes name the selector's `data-*` hook. `selectors` are the `[data-x]` strings records name (hostOf).

### `lib/motion-behaviour-settings.mjs`
- `positionsByTemplate({ reads, nodes, rootComponent })` → the draft's computed position of every root element a template element is, by width; `stickyTiers(by)` → `headerSticky` per tier from those positions, or null when no tier pins.
- `scrolledLooksOf(facts)` → the looks the draft's scrolled state gives each template element (`{ <key>: [ { where, path, by: { <width>: { rest, scrolled } } } ] }`), from the surface states keyed by a `scrolled` state key and each element's `logic.holesByState`; `scrolledThresholdOf(facts)` → the scroll distance the draft's own records state for it (`scrollY > 40`), or null; `paddingBox(value)` → a one-to-four pixel padding shorthand as `{ top, right, bottom, left }`, else null; `scrollShrinkOf(record, ctx)` → a transition of a property the scrolled state changes on its element (`ctx.template.scrolled` and `scrolledAt` from `lib/fill-behaviour.mjs::templateOf`) as `rowShrink` and `rowShrinkPadding` on a row whose padding changes, `scrolledOffset` on its header where the draft's threshold is not 50, and `shrinkWidth` on a logo whose width changes, with `placements` naming each template element and its settings.
- `headerScrollOf(record, ctx)` → the header's scrolled shadow and threshold and, for a pinned header, its sticky behaviour per tier; `dotPulseOf(record, ctx)` → the open-status dot pulse on a live status dot read from the template; `accordionScrollOf(record)` → scrolling to the accordion row just opened; `autoplayOf(record)` → the testimonial slider's autoplay; `pinnedTimelineOf(record, ctx)` → the pinned horizontal timeline (a writer moving a track held in a sticky stage sideways): its track, counter, focus and active year as `sgs/timeline` settings.

- `templateOf(facts)` → the fact record's template as the recognisers read it (`ctx.template`); `effectTemplateOf(facts)` → its committed cut, `EFFECT_TEMPLATE` its file name; `scrollThreshold(record)`, `movesSideways(property)`, `pinnedSectionOf(record, ctx)`, `scrollsToTop(record)`.

### `lib/motion-effect-element.mjs`
- `callPathOf(record)` → the functions an animation record's call path passes through, innermost first; `cssTextDeclarations(formula)` → the declarations a `cssText` formula sets; `effectElementSource(record, records)` → the style record giving a code-created element its declarations, or null; `effectElementStyle(record, records)` → the effect element's declarations for an animation record, or null.
- `colourOf(value)` → a single colour as `{ hex, alpha }`, or null; `largerSideFactor(decl)` → the multiple of its host's larger side a declared length is, or null.

### `lib/motion-record-text.mjs`
- `props`, `nameOf`, `words`, `blob`, `triggerOf`, `durationOf`, `easingOf`: what a record states; `MINUS`, `TIMES`, `NUMBER`, `number`, `round`, `compact`: the number patterns and helpers its formulas are read with.

- `codeTree(text)`, `nodesOf(tree, test)`, `callsOf(tree, name)`, `expressionOf(tree)`, `negativeExpr(node)`, `stringPieces(node)`, `readsScrollY(node)`, `optionKeys(call)`, `optionValue(call, key)`, `cssCallOf(property)`: the syntax-tree readers; `timerMs(record)`; `scrollValueName(property, record)`.

### `lib/motion-tilt.mjs`
- `fromPointer(property)` → whether a pointer handler wrote the property from the pointer's position (its own formula and value only). `tiltOf(record, ctx)` → a script-written rotation from the pointer's position as a tilt (the hover state's `followPointer`) with a glare layer when the same handler writes the pointer position into custom properties; `tiltGlareHostOf(record, ctx)` → the id of the tilt record whose glare a handler of its own writes, or null; `tiltResetOf(record)` → the spring back of a tilt.

### `lib/trace-match.mjs`
- `names`: A record names its element by template_tpl_id, by nearest_tpl_id, or (structural targets) inside element/trace text.
- `durOk`: duration_ms is a number, or text: "per property" (each properties[] entry carries its own duration_ms) or a formula.
- `eventKey`: An event with no template id or no nearest one is keyed '-', never the text "null".
- `matchFor(key, recs, shift)` → the first record whose duration fits the event key's (`durOk`, with `shift`) and which names the key's template or nearest element (`names`), else undefined.

### `tests/fixtures/motion-fixture-db.mjs`
- `motionFixtureDb`: blocks: { 'sgs/x': [ { target, css_element } ] } (the root is always added).

### `lib/census-conservation.mjs`
- `layerTimings(element)` → the timing values one sgsMotion element's layers give each longhand, `{ longhand: [value] }`; a layer that sets no delay runs at 0ms.
- `rootLayerTimings(doc)` → `layerTimings` of the root element only: a part's layer times the part, not the write's element.
- `motionLonghands(w)` → the longhands one motion-pass write sets: the root layer's timing longhands, the write's own property when it names one, else none.
- `layerGives(prop, raw, given, tokens)` → whether a timing longhand's read value is what the layer gives it at every entry of the list (times by ms, easings by canonical spelling, `token:` values through the client's tokens).

### `lib/fill-motion-settle.mjs`
- `motionSettled({ unmapped, writes, nodes, flat, refOf, mdb, db, calFor, reads, rawSnapshot })` → settles by `motion` each raised resting row whose every width equals what the written sgsMotion hover state carries; returns `{ unmapped, answered }`. The surface's rows first pass through `lib/fill-timing.mjs::timingDuplicates`.
- `motionRejudged({ settled, writes, nodes, flat, refOf, mdb, db, calFor, rawSnapshot })` → rejudges a resting timing the element pass settled against the stylesheet by the written layer instead: settled `motion` where every width is a value the layer gives, else an UNMAPPED timing-conflict row; returns `{ settled, unmapped }`.
- `HOVER_PAINT` → the colour and shadow properties every sgsMotion hover state transitions beside its movement.
- `baseTransitions()` → the block parts' own base transitions, which a part's motion `transition` keeps, or null where the generated table is absent.
- `transitionListOutcomes({ nodes, flat, refOf, reads, writes, mdb, db, calFor, base })` → settles a resting transition-property or transition-behavior read where live transitions the draft's properties (the site-look default paint in order, or the written hover state as a set), else an UNMAPPED row naming the difference; returns `{ settled, unmapped }`. A live list that also transitions properties the draft does not is settled too (same reason, the extras named in the detail) when no state look of the element changes any of them at that width, and an inherited one (`lib/calibrate-props.mjs::INHERITED`) also when no look of an ancestor node's targets does; a width with no state read, or a list missing a draft property the movement entries cannot account for, stays raised.

### `lib/fill-state-reach.mjs`
- `stateDrafts` → the draft's state looks per target, grouped by state, pseudo-element and property across the read widths.
- `ancestorLook(reads, rec, target, state, prop)` → the ancestor target whose pointer-state look an inherited property follows, when the element declares no `prop` of its own at any read width; null otherwise.
- `ancestorHolds({ cal, state, slot, prop, ancestor, aprop, taken })` → whether a state setting already written paints the ancestor's `aprop` at its slot, so the element paints no state rule of its own.
- `motionHolds(mdb, rec, target, home)` → whether the block's sgsMotion hover layer holds this target's hover transform, so the state pass leaves it there; a DB without motion tables holds none.

### `lib/form-submit-run.mjs`
- `formSettingsOf(content)` → the form's `{ successMessage, successRedirect, notifyEmail }` from an `sgs_form` post's content (an unset one is ''), or null when it holds no sgs/form block.
- `formFieldsOf(content)` → each field block in the content, `[ { block, label, required, msgRequired } ]` in document order.
- `testValueFor(c)` → a valid test value for a control `{ tag, type, min, options }`: a string, `'check'` to tick it, or null to leave it.
- `successVerdict({ settings, finalUrl, successText })` → whether a submission ended in the form's own success state: the redirect target when it has one, else a visible success message.
- `originalRecipient({ subject, to })` → the address a mail was meant for: the one a test site's redirect names in the subject, else the mail's own `to`.

### `lib/form-submit-page.mjs`
- `FORM_SELECTOR` → `form.sgs-form__inner`; `REQUIRED` → its required controls.
- `markedValueFor(info, marker)` → `testValueFor`'s value, with every free-text control carrying the marker when one is given.
- `fillVisible(page, skip, { marker, form })` → fills the reachable required controls of `form` (a selector; a visually hidden tile through its visible label; never the honeypot), leaving the first `skip` empty; with a marker also its empty free-text fields; returns the required controls it cannot fill (a file field).
- `stepInPage(form)` → `{ at, of, label, decoys }`: the shown `.sgs-form-step` and the visible Next/Continue buttons that are not the form's own.
- `submitForm(page, skip, { marker, form, settleMs })` → walks the form's steps with its own Next (`.sgs-form__button--next`, else a button reading Next or Continue) and clicks its submit button; returns `{ steps, decoys }`; throws `stuck on step N of M ("label")…` when a Next click leaves the shown step unchanged, and when neither a submit nor a next button shows.

### `lib/site-check-report.mjs`
- `CHECKS` → the eight checks `{ id, n, title }`; `parseOnly(raw)` → `{ ids }` or `{ error }`.
- `verdictOf(items)` → `fail` when an item failed or carries an unknown status, `pass` when one passed, else `n-a`; `checkRecord(id, items, naReason)` → the check's record; `exitCodeOf(checks)` → 1 when one failed.
- `skippedRecord(id)` → the record of a check `--only` left out; `evidenceOf(item)` → an item's evidence line (url, selector, screenshot, error, detail).
- `renderMarkdown(result)` → `result.md`: the table by check, the failures with evidence, then every item.

### `lib/site-check-site.mjs`
- `targetOf(site, targets, roots)`, `siteBase(target, roots)` → the target and its `WP_URL_*` (never another secret); `candidateRoots` → the repo, then a worktree's main checkout (re-exported from `scripts/parity/flows/lib/browser.mjs`).
- `STORE_EXAMPLES` → the Store API list a product or product-category row opens its example from.
- `rowsFor(rows, idsSite, target)`, `readRows(repo, client, target)` → the page map with its ids kept for the site that owns them or its mirror.
- `pageTargets(rows, base)` → `{ pages, examples, skipped }`; `flowsClient(outRoot)` → the client `scripts/parity/flows` belongs to, from `scripts/parity/flows/lib/flow.mjs::flowsOutRoot`.
- `assertCheckContact({ site, target, ids, withCart, env })` → throws under `SGS_NO_SITE`, and on a protected target when `ids` holds `forms` or `withCart` is set (the message names the `--only` list of the other checks); page loads pass.

### `lib/site-check-nav.mjs`
- `MARK` → the `data-site-check` attribute the in-page readers mark triggers and targets with.
- `shownInPage(el)` → rendered and not hidden (below the fold counts); `onScreenInPage(el)` → also overlapping the viewport (an opened panel); `stateInPage([mark, trigger, target, src])` → `{ expanded, shown }` of a marked pair.
- `pathKey(href, base)` → origin and path without the trailing slash, for comparing links.
- `readHeaderLinksInPage()` → the header's links with their menu-bar flag; `readDraftLinksInPage()` → the page's links to a `.dc.html` draft file.
- `markMegaInPage(mark)`, `markDrawerInPage(mark)` → mark the visible mega triggers and their panels, the visible burger and its drawer (the burger is the header button whose `aria-controls` names a `<dialog>` printing `data-sgs-nav-modality`, which only sgs/nav-drawer does; the basket's drawer dialog is never taken for it).
- `menuItems({ header, links, pages, examples, headerRows, draftLinks, megaTriggers, base, url })` → the menu check's items; a `sgs_mega_menu` header row passes on the trigger in `megaTriggers` (from `markMegaInPage`) whose panel id ends `-mega-<id>` and whose panel is on the page.
- `headerRowsOf({ rows, loaded, menuLinks })` → the page-map rows in the header menu as `menuItems` takes them; a product or category row carries the draft's link `text` and the resolved `url` (with its query) instead of a page address, so it is matched by them, never by its title. `addressKey(href, base)` → origin, path and query, for comparing a link with a query.
- `megaItems(page, { url, shoot })`, `drawerItem(page, { width, url, shoot })` → one item per mega trigger, one per width.
- `openDisclosure(page, trigger, target)`, `closeDisclosure(page, trigger, target, closer)` → open by hover, focus and ArrowDown, then a click; close by the close button, Escape, then moving away.

### `lib/site-check-parts.mjs`
- `readPartsInPage(mark)` → the page's marked modals, choice flows and forms (a flow inside a closed modal carries `popup: { modal, anchor, visibleTrigger }`, naming that modal's marks); `FLOW_ROOT` → a choice flow's root selector; `flowStateInPage` → its shown step, step count, Back and Continue.
- `missingFlowRows(rows, flows)` → the page-map `sgs_choice_flow` rows no rendered flow shows: a flow naming a slug (`data-flow-slug`) is the row of that slug; a flow naming none is the row its `aria-label` matches.
- `WOO_PAGES` → what the cart, checkout and account pages must show; `wooStateInPage` → whether it shows, else the page's first words.
- `modalItem`, `flowItem`, `formItem`, `wooItem` → one item each (`flowItem` opens a flow's closed modal first, by the same visible trigger `modalItem` uses (`openDisclosure`), checks the flow, then closes the modal, and fails naming the popup when no visible control opens it); `addOneLine(page, base)` → one basket line through the Store API for `--with-cart`.

### `lib/intake-palette-declared.mjs`
- `ROLE_WORDS` → the role vocabulary read from `data/palette-role-words.json`.
- `namespaceOf(names)` → the namespace word most colour tokens share (`mm` in `--mm-cocoa`), or null; kept off alias names before matching.
- `declarations({ tokens, folder, slugs, words })` → every declared role, `[ { slug, hex, token, strength, source: 'alias'|'comment'|'readme', why } ]`.
- `declaredRoles(list)` → the winning (strongest) declaration per slug as a Map, and `conflicts` for ties between different colours, which drop the slug.

### `lib/intake-palette-into.mjs`
- `PALETTE_ONLY_NOTE` → the note a palette-only `intake.json` carries saying the full intake must run for the other stages.
- `rowRoles(r)` → the slugs a palette row proposes: its roles, else its one role, else none.
- `markRoles(mark, oldRow)` → the slugs a mark names on a row, or null when it names none that can be compared.
- `intoIntake({ intake, reviewMd, palette, client, takenOn })` → `{ intake, reviewMd, created, kept, dropped }`: the new palette block put into the current record and review text, keeping a mark only when its slugs equal the new proposal's.

### `lib/intake-palette-run.mjs`
- `writeIntoIntake(at, out, say)` → `--into-intake`: the proposal written into `intake.json` and `review.md` through `intoIntake`.
- `PALETTE_STAGES` → the stages a palette-only run executes: routing, replay, tokens and palette.
- `runPaletteOnly(o, { log })` → runs only those stages for `intake.mjs --palette-only` and returns the palette result.

### `lib/intake-palette-usage.mjs`
- `isBackground(p)` → whether a CSS property is `background` or `background-color`.
- `isBorder(p)` → whether a CSS property is a border or outline property, side and colour forms included.
- `usageRoles(groups, uses)` → the roles the painted usage gives each colour group, from the normalised usage rows; with no text flags every colour row counts as text.

### `lib/origin-file.mjs`
- `draftHashOf(manifest)` → sha256 over every `.dc.html` file's path and hash in a handoff manifest, in path order; null when it lists no template.
- `stampOrigin(origin, hash)` → the origin with every entry stamped with the draft hash; the input is not changed.
- `originVerdict(origin, hash)` → `{ ok, stamped, why }`: ok false when any entry names another hash, stamped false when no entry carries one.
- `readOrigin(originFile, manifestFile)` → reads an origin file and checks it against `MANIFEST.json`; throws when it is from another export; returns `{ origin, verdict }`.

### `lib/resolve-nearest.mjs`
- `encloses(home, slot)` → whether the element at path `home` is the element at `slot` or one of its ancestors; an undefined home encloses nothing.
- `nearestHome(rows, homeOf, slot)` → the tied rows whose home is nearest the read element, or null when no row's home can be compared.

### `lib/resolve-side-effects.mjs`
- `sideEffectFree(rows, { effectsOf, slot, same, siblings, paintOf, equal, isLength })` → the tied rows a side effect does not rule out, or `rows` unchanged when none would remain.

### `lib/fill-list-content.mjs`

- `identityKeys(keys)` → the item keys a block names its items by: string keys the block declares technical whose primary role is identity (`data/item-roles.json`). `withIdentity(built, keys)` → the built items with each empty identity key written as a slug of the item's words, unique in the list (`-2` on a repeat), else `item-<n>`; `listDecisions` runs it, and a list carrying no words is still one row, never items holding only made-up keys.
- `markItemChildren({ nodes, db, schemaOf })` → the skeleton nodes, each node with no child nodes whose block draws its items as child blocks (`listTarget(...).kind` `children`) and has a draft element marked `itemChildren`; `fill.mjs` calls it after `skeletonNodes`, and `lib/fill-read.mjs::jobsFor` reads such a node's text styles off its own element (`own`).
- `currentItemRule(decisions)` → `{ blocks, attr, value }` from `rules.slider` (`settings.visible`, `currentItem.visible`), or null: the setting a slider block takes as `value` when its list is a current-item display (`listItems(...).current`), so one slide shows. `listContentWrites` takes it as `oneAtATime` (default read from `data/skeleton-decisions.json`).

### `shop-fixtures.mjs`
- `FIXTURE_SITES` → the fresh test sites and local mirrors the shop fixtures may be written to (`mamas-test`, `eye-care-clone-test`, `local-mamas`, `local-eye-care`).

### `shop-parts.mjs`
- `themeFiles(vocab, repo)` → the theme files the shop parts vocabulary names, read from the repo.
- `draftSurfaces(client, repo)` → one client's draft surfaces (`lib/shop-parts-read.mjs::readShopSurfaces`), or null when its export has no `surfaces.json`.

### `tests/fixtures/frozen-db/frozen-db.mjs`
- `BLOCKS` → the blocks the frozen tests build or plan.
- `frozenDb()` → builds the frozen slice as a read-only fixture DB and returns its path.
- `sliceOf(db)` → the `blocks`, `block_attributes` and `property_equivalents` rows of a DB, each row's non-null columns only, in a stable order.

### `tests/palette-keys.test.mjs`
- `slugValues(roles, hexOf)` → slug → hex from token → slugs (framework slugs only).
- `compareClient(client)` → one client's proposal compared with its answer key.
- `REVIEW` → every remaining difference, slug → `{ key, proposal, class, check }`; each is a choice of the key that no rendered or code fact reproduces.
- `NAME_ONLY` → the slugs the proposal takes from a token name alone, each a review class.
- `KEY_ONLY` → the key's own slugs that are not in theme.json's palette, slug → the token it names.

### `tools/palette-keys.mjs`
- `keyFile(client)` → the path of a client's `palette-key.json`.
- `fromMarks(client)` → token → slugs from Bean's palette marks in `review.md`.
- `fromSnapshot(client)` → token → the snapshot slugs whose colour equals the token's value.
- `derive(client, source)` → `fromMarks` or `fromSnapshot` by the `source` name, else null.
